account: The patron chartered the expedition: package the expedition framework so it is reusable and distributable without calcifying into the prescriptive process it replaces. Charter drafted and settled during planning.

Restructured the repo into the layered layout; moved both canon narratives into code/ byte-for-byte (diffs empty against approved revisions); wrote README covering the layer model, adoption path, and amendment discipline; extended AGENTS.md with layout and amendment discipline while preserving the original contributor rules.
B1 — structure and canon. The company rests with the repo restructured and the canon verified unchanged.

B2 — templates. Charter, dispatch, and journal-entry templates written, each a page or less, fields drawn from what the narratives already name. Checked against guardrail 1: they name contents, never steps.

Wrote the journey-state spec, JSON Schema, a full example log (river-gate: failed crossing, rider/word exchange, arrival), and a stdlib-only validator that reads the schema as source of truth. Example and self-build logs validate; an intentionally malformed line fails with seven distinct errors.
B3 — journey-state substrate specified, exampled, and validatable.

B4 — skill adapter. Self-contained adapters/claude/ skill written (roles, resume-or-charter, log-primary events, Voice section, provenance note); project-snippet fallback written; build-skill produces expedition.skill with the expedition/SKILL.md zip structure and a self-containment check that fails the build on any ../ reference.

Built the map rendering: tools/render embeds journey events into a self-contained HTML template (inline CSS/JS, no external fetches) showing planned route faint, actual path over it, basecamps as nodes, failed crossings as dead-end spurs, riders as branches to the patron's band, terminal state marked. Rendered the river-gate example and this log together and verified visually in a browser. Wrote spec/analysis.md with the descriptive questions the corpus can answer and the guardrail that analytics never flow back to the agent.
B5 — map rendering and analysis notes complete.
Closing dispatch sent to the patron: all basecamps reached, one detour (file:// preview), landmarks recorded, one rider carried home.

Canon wording for the scout clarification proposed in the closing dispatch; the sentence is the patron's to approve before it enters code/frontiersman.md. Also carried home: publishing and distribution decisions, and whether the built expedition.skill zip is committed or built on demand.

B6 — dogfood. This log kept from B1 onward (B1 retroactive by minutes), validated with tools/validate, rendered with tools/render into expeditions/self-build/map.html. Journal entry inked: what fought back, what the templates failed to express, open questions.

Arrival as chartered: layered structure with canon unchanged; journey-state substrate specified, exampled, and validatable; skill adapter self-contained with zero target-project configuration; map rendering replays a journey.jsonl visually; the framework dogfooded on its own construction. The rider on canon wording and publishing awaits the patron's word.
The patron answered the canon rider.
answer: Write the narrative for the scout and weave it thoughtfully into the canon.

account: Canon amended under the patron's word: wrote code/scout.md — the scout's narrative (sent not self-sent, bounded errand, report the land not the hope, return with less blank space; the scout finds, the frontiersman decides) — and added the commission/accountability sentence to the frontiersman's scout section. Propagated the third canon file through README, AGENTS.md, the skill, and the project snippet; rebuilt expedition.skill.

The patron refined the scout narrative: the scout must not be pressured to always return an answer — returning a report is the accomplishment, even when that report calls for more scouts or further surveying.
answer: Rephrase the return line so the scout owes a report, not an answer.

account: Amended code/scout.md per the patron's word: the return line now reads 'The scout owes the company a report, not an answer; a report that calls for another rider has still moved the map.' Also aligned the closing charge from 'bring the answer home unbent' to 'bring the account home unbent' so the closing does not reintroduce the pressure the patron removed. Rebuilt the skill; vendored copy matches.

The patron approved adding a glossary to the code: plain-language descriptions of every weight-bearing term in the metaphor, explicitly without operational definitions, to keep the canon aligned and terminology consistent over time.
answer: Add code/glossary.md — plain-language, in-metaphor descriptions only, no operational definitions.

account: Wrote code/glossary.md: twenty-three weight-bearing terms grouped by roles, country, setting out, trail, word between camp and home, record, and coming home. Each entry a one-or-two-sentence plain-language gloss inside the metaphor; the file states its own subordination (where it disagrees with a narrative, it is wrong) and that adding a term is a canon change. Propagated through README, AGENTS.md, and the skill; rebuilt expedition.skill.

The patron judged the glossary too process-like for the canon: a reference table in code/ changes the folder's character. Agreed to remove it from the canon and carry its substance into spec/ as a lexicon.
answer: Remove glossary.md from the canon; move its substance to spec/ as a lexicon.

account: Removed code/glossary.md; wrote spec/lexicon.md carrying the same plain-language glosses, now each traced to the narrative section that defines it, with the subordination rule, the closed-list rule, and an explicit ban on operational definitions. The canon is narratives only again; AGENTS.md now says so. Lexicon added to the skill's vendored spec via build-skill; skill rebuilt.

At the patron's word, the repository came under git: initial commit of the full state, 32 files. Build artifacts (expedition.skill, rendered maps) are ignored, not committed — built on demand, per the open question in the journal, resolvable later if the patron prefers them tracked.
